claim: DR47-14 clause 5, added by the previous revision, short-circuits the mutated arm of acceptances 46 and 54, so both rows' Path clause (iii) is false and both state a RED value the mutation cannot produce. 46 additionally rules out by name the only assertion that actually moves. NOTE: the architect lane returned PASS at this same hash, with no must-fix.
evidence: Clause 5 adds a capture-phase pointerdown on stage.ownerDocument whose whole body is to invalidate reorderTrackerRef, bound inside beginTravelRecording and removed by the same stop(). Capture runs ancestor-first, so on press 2 it fires BEFORE onPointerSuppress. Acceptances 46 and 54 both mutate by restoring the un-split early return (clause 1 reverted), against a fixture whose gesture 1 lost its terminals — so the recording is live and clause 5's listener is attached. Under that mutation the early return fires without re-seeding, and the tracker clause 5 just cleared is never re-established. The plan's own acceptance 58 states the mechanism: reorderTrackerRef has exactly two other writers, the seeding site and clause 1's re-seed, and BOTH live inside beginTravelRecording. So the mutated arm of 46 issues ZERO POSTs, not exactly one POST carrying A's oid; the mutated arm of 54 reports no live subject, not A's subject and press point. 46 explicitly forbids the substitution the lane will actually observe, naming a request COUNT as non-discriminating. All 94 code anchors resolve exactly once, so the defect is in the plan's reasoning, not its citations.
impact: 46 is the phase's designated must-be-shown-RED gate at S47-4 and, per pre-mortem S7, the only gate proving a lost terminal cannot commit against an element the user never touched for the ordinary-arm press class. As written, driving 46's mutation no longer reproduces the wrong-subject write hazard at all — it reproduces a dead press — so the row measures clause 1's usability property while being presented as the phase's write-safety gate, and the criterion's own do-not-substitute-the-count instruction puts the S47-4 lane in a contradiction at the exact commit where the write lands. This is the plan's own Path clause (iii) failing on the row that matters most, introduced by the round that added clause 5.
required_correction: Re-state 46 and 54 against the tree that now includes clause 5. Either (i) make the mutation COMPOUND — revert clause 1 and remove clause 5's pointerdown invalidation — so the mutated arm genuinely reaches the A-write, saying why no single mutation reaches it, exactly as acceptance 41 already argues for its own compound mutation; or (ii) keep the single mutation and restate the first-moving assertion as the POST count or tracker liveness, deleting the count-does-not-discriminate note and re-stating what the row then proves — noting that under (ii) the plan no longer holds a gate over the write landing on B rather than A under a single mutation, which must be said in S47-4's must-be-shown-RED set and in pre-mortem S7. Either way, correct section 3.2b's claim that the five clauses are independent with none load-bearing alone: clause 5 now subsumes clause 1's wrong-subject hazard on the ordinary-arm path, leaving clause 1 load-bearing for the dead-press argument rather than for S7. Re-run the Path re-sweep over every row that assumes a surviving tracker across a press; the critic checked 50, 52, 55 and 58-60 and found them unaffected, so 46 and 54 are the two that move.
